1	Sprint Backlog — Autonomous AI Code Trust System
     2	Sprint goal: Build a working, plug-and-play system that takes a GitHub repository, reconstructs development context, identifies the code's fingerprint, predicts likely failure modes, and autonomously discovers reproducible bugs in code that already compiles and passes existing tests.
     3	
     4	The system must work with Git history alone, while supporting AI development conversations as an additional source of intelligence.
     5	
     6	Target demo: Tieto's AI-modified MessagePack C# repository.
     7	
     8	P0 — Must Complete
     9	ID	Task	Deliverable
    10	1	Repository ingestion	Clone repository, select base/target commits, extract diffs, commit history, tests, and dependencies.
    11	2	Code fingerprinting engine ⭐	Identify structural, semantic, behavioral, and historical characteristics of modified code.
    12	3	Fingerprint → failure-pattern matching ⭐	Map detected fingerprints to known bug classes and suitable testing strategies.
    13	4	Development Memory	Store Git evidence, requirements, assumptions, code relationships, and investigation results with provenance.
    14	5	Context ingestion	Import AI conversations, prompts, decisions, and tool execution history when available.
    15	6	Context retrieval	Retrieve relevant evidence without loading entire conversations into the LLM context window.
    16	7	Git history archaeology	Identify previous bug fixes, behavioral changes, and potentially fragile code regions.
    17	8	Autonomous investigation planner	Generate bug hypotheses, prioritize them, and choose appropriate testing techniques.
    18	9	Executable bug discovery	Generate and execute differential, property-based, boundary, and stateful tests.
    19	10	Counterfactual debugging	Compare historical implementations and isolate changes responsible for observed failures.
    20	11	Bug verification	Reproduce failures, minimize counterexamples, and distinguish genuine bugs from intended behavior.
    21	12	Evidence-backed reporting	Generate reports containing the suspected cause, triggering input, execution evidence, and reproducible test.
    22	13	MCP integration	Expose repository analysis, bug hunting, and findings retrieval to coding agents.
    23	14	End-to-end demonstration	Run the system against at least one provided MessagePack branch and demonstrate its findings.
    24	P0 Feature Spotlight: Code Fingerprinting
    25	This is the feature I would prioritize alongside the autonomous investigator.
    26	
    27	The goal is to recognize what kind of code you're looking at and what kinds of failures are most likely to occur in that code.
    28	
    29	A fingerprint should describe more than the programming language or framework.
    30	
    31	Fingerprint dimensions
    32	Dimension	What to detect	Potential failure modes
    33	Structural	Recursion, complex branching, nested loops, generics	Stack overflow, missed branches, type-handling errors
    34	Memory	Buffer manipulation, pooling, shared references	Corruption, aliasing, use-after-disposal
    35	State	Mutable objects, caches, state machines	State leakage, invalid transitions
    36	Concurrency	Async operations, locks, shared state	Races, deadlocks, ordering bugs
    37	Data handling	Serialization, parsing, conversions	Overflow, malformed input, encoding errors
    38	Boundary	Index arithmetic, size calculations, integer casts	Off-by-one errors, truncation
    39	Historical	Previous fixes, refactors, optimization commits	Regressions in previously fragile behavior

   117	B — Development Memory	AI context ingestion, evidence storage, retrieval, PR context preservation	4, 5, 6, 15, 16
   118	C — Autonomous Bug Hunter	Hypothesis generation, test execution, counterfactual debugging, verification	8, 9, 10, 11, 18–21

   139	    }

   141	  "experiments": [],

   144	This allows the fingerprinting, memory, and bug-hunting components to be developed independently.
   145	
   146	Sprint Acceptance Criteria
   147	The sprint is successful when:
   148	
   149	[ ] A repository can be analyzed without AI conversation history.
   150	[ ] The system extracts a meaningful code fingerprint from modified components.
   151	[ ] Fingerprints map to specific failure hypotheses and testing strategies.
   152	[ ] Git history contributes evidence to the investigation.
   153	[ ] Optional AI context can be ingested and queried without sending the entire history to an LLM.
   154	[ ] The investigator generates and executes tests autonomously.
   155	[ ] A suspected bug is reproduced and reduced to a minimal failing example.
   156	[ ] Reports distinguish confirmed bugs from unverified hypotheses.
   157	[ ] An MCP client can trigger an investigation.
   158	[ ] The end-to-end pipeline runs against a Tieto MessagePack branch.
   159	Demo fallback: If no genuine bug is found in the available time, use a clearly labeled, deliberately injected regression to demonstrate the full pipeline. Don't present synthetic defects as discoveries in the original code.
   160	
   161	The Five Features That Should Define the Demo
   162	1. Code DNA: Fingerprint a code change and identify the failure modes most relevant to it.
   163	
   164	2. Development Memory: Reconstruct intent from Git history and optional AI context.
   165	
   166	3. Context Intelligence: Retrieve precise evidence without consuming the agent's entire context window.
   167	
   168	4. Autonomous Bug Investigation: Generate hypotheses, design experiments, and discover reproducible counterexamples.
   169	
   170	5. Collective Failure Intelligence: Preserve verified failure patterns so future agents can investigate similar code more effectively.
   171	
   172	The distinctive demo is not a dashboard with a trust score. It's showing the system recognize a risky code pattern, connect it to historical evidence, formulate a specific failure hypothesis, execute an experiment that exposes a hidden bug, and preserve that discovery for future investigations.

---

1	# DEMO — runnable script
     2	
     3	Every command below has been run on this machine. Copy-paste order, ~6 minutes.
     4	
     5	Prerequisites: Python 3.11+, .NET 8 SDK, the target repo cloned at `./repo`.
     6	
     7	---
     8	
     9	## Beat 0 — The reviewer that was confidently wrong (90 s)
    10	
    11	**Claim to the audience:** an AI reviewer with no provenance discipline produced
    12	a false finding on these very branches, during this project.
    13	
    14	It reported that all four agentic branches re-applied a dependency bump the
    15	maintainers had deliberately reverted, and it cited a real commit:
    16	`d62699e7 "Rollback package dependency versions for analyzers"`. Plausible,
    17	specific, evidence-backed — and **false**.
    18	
    19	The cause was one unrecorded assumption: *"the merge-base is the base."*
    20	`origin/develop` does not exist in this fork, so the fallback silently used
    21	`master` and every diff started two commits too early.
    22	
    23	```bash
    24	cd repo
    25	git rev-parse origin/ju26-issue-2283^          # 32258fdb  <- the real base
    26	git merge-base origin/ju26-issue-2283 origin/master   # 524fd55e  <- off by two
    27	git rev-parse --verify origin/develop          # fails: the ref does not exist
    28	cd ..
    29	```
    30	
    31	**The point:** the diff never changes, but the conclusion drawn from it does.
    32	Base resolution is an assumption, and unrecorded assumptions are where
    33	hallucinations come from.
    34	
    35	---
    36	
    37	## Beat 1 — Base resolution as a checked assumption (60 s)
    38	
    39	The resolver computes the base several independent ways, refuses to pick a
    40	winner silently when they disagree, and validates against an external oracle —
    41	the challenge brief's own file counts.
    42	
    43	```bash
    44	cd trust/ingest
    45	python base_resolver.py --repo ../../repo --all-ju26 \
    46	    --expect-files 2283=4,2234=4,2129=28,2297=237 \
    47	    --json ../../.trust/bases.json
    48	```
    49	
    50	Observed output: all four branches resolve to `32258fdb`, each flagged
    51	`methods disagree` (reproducing the exact failure condition as a *detected*
    52	dispute), then confirmed by the oracle — 4, 4, 28, 237 changed files, matching
    53	the brief exactly.
    54	
    55	---
    56	
    57	## Beat 2 — A real hidden problem in Tieto's branch (3 min)
    58	
    59	This is the centrepiece: a genuine defect in AI-authored code that **compiles,
    60	passes every test, and no reviewer would catch in a 237-file diff.**
    61	
    62	```bash
    63	cd ../assumptions
    64	python tfm_guard_check.py \
    65	    --repo ../../repo \
    66	    --branch origin/ju26-issue-2297 \
    67	    --base 32258fdb \
    68	    --issue-text ../../.trust/issues/2297.md \
    69	    --json ../../.trust/findings/2297-tfm-guard.json
    70	```
    71	
    72	### What it finds
    73	
    74	Branch `ju26-issue-2297` implements issue #2297, *"Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage
    75	attribute to generated code."* The agent did most of this **well**: all six T4
    76	templates updated, all 222 verified snapshots regenerated consistently, `.tt`
    77	and generated `.cs` kept in sync. Say so — it earns the finding credibility.
    78	
    79	But it wrapped the attribute in a guard of its own invention:
    80	
    81	```csharp
    82	#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK
    83	    [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]
    84	#endif
    85	```
    86	
    87	That guard asserts an unstated assumption: *the attribute is unavailable on
    88	netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework.* The tool falsifies it by compiling the
    89	attribute, unguarded, against those exact frameworks:
    90	
    91	| Probe | Result |
    92	|---|---|
    93	| `netstandard2.0` | **COMPILES** |
    94	| `net472` | **COMPILES** |
    95	
    96	So the premise is false, and the consequence is a silent feature gap:
    97	
    98	| Fact | Value |
    99	|---|---|
   100	| TFMs the library ships | `netstandard2.0`, `netstandard2.1`, `net8.0`, `net472` |
   101	| TFMs the tests cover | `net8.0` only |
   102	| TFMs silently excluded | `netstandard2.0`, `net472` |
   103	| Test-observable | **No** |
   104	
   105	**Two of the four shipped target frameworks never receive the feature the issue
   106	asked for.**
   107	
   108	### Why no test catches it
   109	
   110	1. All eight test projects target `net8.0`, where the guard always passes. CI
   111	   never compiles the excluded path.
   112	2. The 222 verified snapshots were regenerated *with* the guard, so the
   113	   snapshot tests now assert the guarded output is correct. **The tests codify
   114	   the gap.**
   115	
   116	### Why it is not merely a style preference
   117	
   118	```bash
   119	cd ../../repo
   120	# the guard is not a repo convention - it did not exist at the base
   121	git grep -c 'NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK' 32258fdb || echo "0 occurrences at base"
   122	# the repo's CI already consumes this attribute - the feature has a real client
   123	grep -n 'ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute' azure-pipelines/test.runsettings
   124	cd ..
   125	```
   126	
   127	And the issue text (`.trust/issues/2297.md`) settles intent. The request:
   128	*"I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage
   129	attribute."* Unconditional. **Neither the issue nor either of its two comments
   130	mentions any target framework.** The conditionality came from the implementer,
   131	not the request.
   132	
   133	### Verify it yourself — the whole point
   134	
   135	The tool keeps its probe projects on disk precisely so this works:
   136	
   137	```bash
   138	dotnet build ".trust/probes/origin_ju26-issue-2297/probe_netstandard2_0/p.csproj" -v q --nologo
   139	# Build succeeded.  0 Error(s)
   140	```
   141	
   142	Nothing above is taken on the reviewer's word.
   143	
   144	### It does not cry wolf
   145	
   146	```bash
   147	cd trust/assumptions
   148	for b in 2283 2234 2129; do
   149	  python tfm_guard_check.py --repo ../../repo --branch origin/ju26-issue-$b --base 32258fdb
   150	done
   151	# "no introduced target-framework guards in this diff"  x3
   152	```
   153	
   154	---
   155	
   156	## Beat 3 — Ask any line why it exists (90 s)
   157	
   158	With the author's session captured, the repo becomes interrogable per line.
   159	
   160	```bash
   161	cd ../session_graph
   162	python why_lines.py --list
   163	python why_lines.py --file build_graph.py --line 592
   164	```
   165	
   166	Returns the exact edit, its timestamp and transcript uuid, the stated reason,
   167	what triggered it, and which human request it serves — plus
   168	`replay matches disk exactly - attribution is complete`.
   169	
   170	**State the limit out loud:** `L4 PRIVATE` is unavailable. Claude Code stores
   171	`thinking` blocks with empty text and a signature only (36 blocks, 0 characters
   172	in this session). We recover what the agent *recorded*, not what it privately
   173	reasoned. So the question answered is *"what reason was recorded for this line,
   174	and does it hold up?"* — which is auditable — not *"what truly caused it?"*,
   175	which is not.
   176	
   177	Then show it refusing to over-claim:
   178	
   179	```bash
   180	python why_lines.py --file ../../DESIGN.md --all
   181	```
   182	
   183	Regions touched by untracked shell writes are reported as divergent, and
   184	narration covering several edits is flagged `[batch]` rather than attributed to
   185	single lines.
   186	
   187	---
   188	
   189	## Beat 4 — The fused graph (60 s)
   190	
   191	```bash

1	# DESIGN — `trust`: Autonomous AI Code Trust System
     2	
     3	**Challenge:** How can AI review code made by AI so that humans can trust it?
     4	**Target:** `junction26-messagepack-csharp`, four agentic branches sharing base
     5	`32258fdb` ("Bump PolySharp from 1.14.1 to 1.15.0").
     6	**Backlog:** `sprints.md` (unchanged; this doc is the architecture that delivers it).
     7	
     8	> **Base-commit note.** `origin/develop` does not exist in this fork, so
     9	> `git merge-base <branch> origin/develop` fails and a naive fallback to
    10	> `master` yields `524fd55e` — a commit two steps too far back. Diffing from
    11	> there attributes two pre-existing dependency commits to the agents. The
    12	> brief's own file counts (4, 4, 28, 237) are the oracle: they match only
    13	> against `32258fdb`. Base resolution is therefore a recorded, verified
    14	> assumption in this system, never a silent fallback. See §5.0 — this error
    15	> happened to us, and catching it is the demo's opening beat.
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## 1. The Trust Contract
    20	
    21	This is the concept the demo defends. Everything below serves it.
    22	
    23	> **The system never asks you to believe it.** Every claim is either (a) a
    24	> reproducible experiment you can re-run with one command, or (b) explicitly
    25	> labeled an unverified hypothesis. There is nothing in between.
    26	
    27	Three enforced properties:
    28	
    29	1. **Proposer / verifier separation.** The LLM proposes hypotheses and *writes*
    30	   experiments. Only *executed code* produces verdicts. An LLM has no code path
    31	   by which it can promote a hypothesis to a finding.
    32	2. **Provenance on every fact.** Every assertion carries an evidence ID that
    33	   resolves to a git object, a `file:line`, an issue URL, or an execution log.
    34	   No unsourced claims enter a report.
    35	3. **Falsifiable output.** Findings ship as standalone runnable tests. The
    36	   human's trust check is `dotnet test`, not reading prose.
    37	4. **Assumptions are reviewed, not just output.** A hallucination is an
    38	   assumption that was never checked. The author's assumptions are captured as
    39	   explicit propositions and each one is attacked against the repo. An
    40	   assumption that survives is a documented warrant; one that falls is a
    41	   hidden defect that no test in the repo covers.
    42	
    43	This is why an AI reviewer can be trusted where an AI author cannot: it is
    44	structurally incapable of asserting a defect it has not demonstrated. And it is
    45	why reviewing *with* the author's context beats reviewing the diff alone — the
    46	diff shows what changed, the context shows what the author believed, and only
    47	the second can be proven wrong.
    48	
    49	---
    50	
    51	## 2. Stack (decided)
    52	
    53	| Layer | Choice | Why |
    54	|---|---|---|
    55	| Orchestrator | Python 3.11+ | Fastest to build; official MCP SDK; LLM SDKs |
    56	| C# parsing | `tree-sitter-c-sharp` | Real ASTs without needing .NET; pip-installable |
    57	| Build/execute | `dotnet` CLI subprocess | .NET 8 SDK (`8.0.4xx`, per `global.json`) |
    58	| Memory | SQLite + FTS5 (stdlib) | Zero deps; full-text evidence retrieval |
    59	| Patterns | YAML | Declarative, shareable, reviewable by humans |
    60	| CLI | Typer | `trust hunt . --base main` |
    61	| LLM | Claude (Opus 5 / Sonnet 5.5) | Hypothesis authoring + experiment synthesis |
    62	
    63	Fallback if the tree-sitter grammar won't install: regex heuristics behind the
    64	same `Fingerprinter` interface. The interface is the seam; the parser is not.
    65	
    66	**Gate:** .NET 8 SDK is not installed on the dev machine. Stages 1–5 and 9–11
    67	below do not need it. Stages 6–8 do.
    68	
    69	---
    70	
    71	## 3. Pipeline
    72	
    73	```
    74	repo + base..target
    75	      |
    76	 [1] ingest ---------> ChangeSet        (hunks, symbols, tests, deps)
    77	      |
    78	 [2] fingerprint ----> Fingerprint[]    (8 dimensions, AST-derived)
    79	      |
    80	 [3] match ----------> Pattern[]        (fingerprint -> bug class -> strategy)
    81	      |
    82	 [4] archaeology ----> Evidence[]       (prior fixes, reverts, churn, fragility)
    83	      |
    84	 [5] plan -----------> Hypothesis[]     (ranked, each citing evidence IDs)
    85	      |
    86	 [6] route ----------> Experiment[]     <== THE HYBRID ROUTER
    87	      |                differential | property | boundary | stateful
    88	      |
    89	 [7] execute --------> Observation[]    (dotnet test, sandboxed, capped)
    90	      |
    91	 [8] verify ---------> Verdict[]        (reproduce xN, shrink, adjudicate)
    92	      |
    93	 [9] report ---------> Finding[]        (+ runnable test artifact)
    94	      |
    95	[10] memory ---------> persisted, retrievable, provenanced
    96	      |
    97	[11] MCP / CLI / dashboard
    98	```
    99	
   100	---
   101	
   102	## 4. Modules
   103	
   104	### `trust.ingest` — sprint #1
   105	
   106	Open or clone the repo; resolve `base`/`target` (default: merge-base). Extract
   107	per-file hunks, changed symbol names, the test inventory, and the dependency
   108	manifest diff. Output: `ChangeSet`.
   109	
   110	Noise triage lands here: classify each changed file as `source`, `generated`
   111	(`*.g.cs`, `*.verified.*`), `test`, `build-config`, or `doc`. Issue #2297 is
   112	237 files of which 16 are semantically meaningful — the reviewer must not
   113	drown, and the ratio itself is reportable.
   114	
   115	### `trust.fingerprint` — sprint #2 (starred)
   116	
   117	Per changed symbol, derive the eight dimensions from `sprints.md`:
   118	
   119	| Dimension | AST / git signals |
   120	|---|---|
   121	| Structural | recursion, loop nesting depth, branch count, type parameters |
   122	| Memory | `ArrayPool`, `IBufferWriter`, `Rent`/`Return`, `stackalloc`, `ref struct`, `Span<T>` |
   123	| State | mutable fields, statics, caches, `IDisposable` |
   124	| Concurrency | `async`/`Task`, `lock`, `Interlocked`, `volatile` |
   125	| Data handling | serialization entry points, `BitConverter`, encoding, conversions |
   126	| Boundary | index arithmetic, `Length`/`Count` math, narrowing casts, `unchecked` |
   127	| Historical | prior fix density on these lines, revert commits, churn |
   128	| AI provenance | commit author, trailers, model/agent identity when present |
   129	
   130	The LLM may *label and explain* a fingerprint. It may not invent a dimension
   131	value that the AST does not support. Fingerprints are claims about code shape,
   132	and they are checkable.
   133	
   134	### `trust.patterns` — sprint #3 (starred; seeds #25)
   135	
   136	Declarative library mapping fingerprint predicates to bug classes and testing
   137	strategies:
   138	
   139	```yaml
   140	- id: buffer-ownership-after-return
   141	  when:
   142	    any_of: [memory.pooling, memory.buffer_writer]
   143	  bug_classes: [use_after_return, double_return, aliasing]
   144	  strategies: [differential, stateful]
   145	  priority: high
   146	
   147	- id: narrowing-cast-on-length
   148	  when:
   149	    all_of: [boundary.narrowing_cast, boundary.length_arithmetic]
   150	  bug_classes: [truncation, integer_overflow, off_by_one]
   151	  strategies: [boundary, property]
   152	  priority: high
   153	```
   154	
   155	Human-reviewable, repo-independent, and the unit that gets shared in #25.
   156	
   157	### `trust.memory` — sprints #4, #5, #6, #22
   158	
   159	SQLite. Tables: `evidence`, `hypotheses`, `experiments`, `observations`,
   160	`verdicts`, `findings` — every row carrying `source`, `provenance`, `created_at`.
   161	Retrieval (#6) is FTS5 + symbol-scoped lookup returning **cited snippets**, never
   162	whole conversations: the agent's context window stays small and every retrieved
   163	line keeps its origin. AI conversation ingestion (#5) is an optional adapter
   164	over the same schema, so the pipeline runs identically with or without it.
   165	
   166	### `trust.capsule` — sprint #15 (PR Intent Capsules)
   167	
   168	Attaches the author agent's context to the repo so a reviewer can read it. One
   169	capsule per branch, committed as `.trust/capsules/<branch>.json`, built from
   170	whichever sources exist:
   171	
   172	| Source | Yields | Available for the four branches? |
   173	|---|---|---|
   174	| Agent session transcript | prompts, tool trail, decisions, rejected options | only if we instrument the agent (see §5.1) |
   175	| Issue text | stated requirements | yes |
   176	| Commit + diff | changed symbols, scope | yes |
   177	| Git history | the author's implicit base, prior art on these lines | yes |
   178	
   179	`trust/session_graph/` already implements the transcript path. It turns a Claude
   180	Code session into a provenanced graph — `PROMPT`, `DECISION` (with the options
   181	the human *rejected*), `TOOL_CALL`, `FILE`, `COMMIT`, `BRANCH` — joined to real
   182	git objects by `inspects` and `parent_of` edges. Extraction is deterministic, so
   183	every capsule field resolves to a transcript `uuid` or a commit SHA.
   184	
   185	When no transcript exists, a **retro-capsule** is reconstructed from issue +
   186	commit + diff and labelled `reconstructed: true`. Reconstructed fields are never
   187	presented as the author's actual reasoning.
   188	
   189	### `trust.assumptions` — the mechanism that removes hallucinations
   190	
   191	The capsule's most valuable content is not what the agent did but what it
   192	*took for granted*. Each assumption becomes a checkable proposition:
   193	
   194	```json
   195	{
   196	  "id": "A3",
   197	  "statement": "the branch's base is the merge-base with the default branch",
   198	  "source": {"transcript_uuid": "ecfcfdfb-...", "kind": "implicit_in_tool_call"},
   199	  "check": "git rev-parse <branch>^ == <assumed_base>",
   200	  "verdict": "FALSIFIED",
   201	  "evidence": "branch parent is 32258fdb; assumed base was 524fd55e",
   202	  "consequence": "two pre-existing commits attributed to the agent"
   203	}
   204	```
   205	
   206	Verdicts: `SUPPORTED` | `FALSIFIED` | `UNCHECKABLE`. The pipeline:
   207	
   208	1. **Harvest** — pull assumptions from the capsule. Explicit ones come from the
   209	   agent's own statements; implicit ones from the shape of its actions (a tool
   210	   call that uses `merge-base` *assumes* the merge-base is the base).
   211	2. **Compile to a check** — each assumption must reduce to a command, a query
   212	   against the graph, or a generated test. An assumption that cannot be reduced
   213	   is `UNCHECKABLE` and is reported as such, not quietly dropped.
   214	3. **Execute** — run it. This is `trust.execute`, reused.
   215	4. **Escalate** — every `FALSIFIED` assumption becomes a hypothesis for the
   216	   bug-hunter, pre-aimed at the code the assumption justified.
   217	
   218	This is the join between the two halves of the system: **the capsule aims the
   219	hunter, and the hunter proves what the capsule only suspected.** Context without
   220	execution is just more prose to distrust; execution without context hunts
   221	blindly. The fingerprint says what *kind* of bug is likely; the falsified
   222	assumption says *where the author was already wrong*.
   223	
   224	### `trust.planner` — sprint #8
   225	
   226	Ranked hypotheses from fingerprints + matched patterns + historical evidence.
   227	Each: failure mode, rationale citing evidence IDs, chosen strategy, **expected
   228	observation** (stated before execution, so the experiment can falsify it).
   229	Rank = pattern priority x historical fragility x blast radius.
   230	
   231	### `trust.router` — the hybrid (sprint #3 + #20)
   232	
   233	Picks an executor per hypothesis, constrained by what is actually available:
   234	
   235	| Strategy | Used when | Oracle |
   236	|---|---|---|
   237	| `differential` | a base build exists | base behavior — no oracle needed |
   238	| `property` | an invariant is stateable | LLM-authored, must survive `verify` |
   239	| `boundary` | index/cast arithmetic detected | derived boundary values |
   240	| `stateful` | mutable/pooled/disposable state | operation-sequence invariants |
   241	
   242	`differential` is preferred whenever available: the divergence *is* the
   243	evidence, so nothing in the verdict can be hallucinated. The others widen reach
   244	to absolute bugs — at the cost of an oracle that `verify` must then defend.
   245	Adaptive selection (#20) re-ranks remaining hypotheses from observed results.
   246	
   247	### `trust.execute` — sprint #9
   248	
   249	Synthesize a standalone xUnit project referencing the target (and for
   250	`differential`, the base) assemblies. Build and run via `dotnet test` in the
   251	scratchpad, never in the repo. Wall-clock timeout, output cap, no network.
   252	
   253	### `trust.verify` — sprint #11
   254	
   255	The gate that makes findings trustworthy:
   256	
   257	1. **Reproduce xN** — anything non-deterministic is `flaky`, not a bug.
   258	2. **Shrink** — reduce to a minimal counterexample.
   259	3. **Adjudicate** — genuine defect vs. intended behavior, checked against
   260	   docs, the issue text, and git history evidence.
   261	
   262	Verdict is one of `confirmed` | `intended` | `flaky` | `inconclusive`.
   263	`confirmed` **requires** an attached reproducible artifact. There is no path to
   264	`confirmed` through LLM assertion alone.
   265	
   266	### `trust.report` — sprint #12
   267	
   268	Every finding carries: suspected cause, minimal triggering input, exact
   269	command, observed vs. expected, evidence chain with provenance, and a
   270	standalone runnable test file. Confirmed findings and unverified hypotheses are
   271	rendered in visually distinct sections and never merged into one score.
   272	
   273	### `trust.mcp` / `trust.cli` — sprints #13, #23
   274	
   275	MCP tools: `analyze_repo`, `get_fingerprints`, `hunt`, `get_findings`,
   276	`recall_evidence`. CLI: `trust hunt . --base main`.
   277	
   278	---
   279	
   280	## 5. Demo — "better debuggable, before vs. after"
   281	
   282	The deliverable is a measured A/B, not a tour of features. Same repo, same
   283	branches, same reviewer engine; the only variable is **whether the author
   284	agent's context is attached**.
   285	
   286	| | Arm A — "before" | Arm B — "after" |
   287	|---|---|---|
   288	| Input | the diff only | diff + Intent Capsule + git archaeology + session graph |
   289	| Represents | code review as practised today | review with the author's reasoning attached |
   290	| Retrieval | read files until you understand | targeted queries against the graph |
   291	
   292	### 5.0 Opening beat: it already happened to us (30 seconds)
   293	
   294	While analysing these four branches, this project's own AI reviewer produced a
   295	confident, evidence-citing finding that all four agents had re-applied a
   296	dependency bump the maintainers deliberately reverted. It cited a real commit
   297	(`d62699e7` "Rollback package dependency versions for analyzers"). It was
   298	**wrong**: `origin/develop` does not exist in this fork, the `merge-base`
   299	fallback silently used `master`, and the diff therefore started two commits too
   300	early. The agents never touched that file.
   301	
   302	One unchecked assumption — "the merge-base is the base" — produced a plausible
   303	false finding. What caught it was not re-reading the diff; it was the
   304	`parent_of` edge in the session graph showing the branch's real parent. This is
   305	the entire thesis in one slide, and it is not synthetic.
   306	
   307	### 5.1 Produce genuine agent context
   308	
   309	Tieto did not ship the agent conversations, so we generate a real pair.
   310	Instrument an agent re-implementing issue **#2283** against base `32258fdb`,
   311	capturing the full session. That yields a diff *and* its authentic capsule, and
   312	lets us compare our agent's solution against Tieto's on the same issue.
   313	
   314	For Tieto's four branches, build retro-capsules (labelled `reconstructed`).
   315	
   316	### 5.2 The measured comparison
   317	
   318	Both arms run the same fingerprint → plan → route → execute → verify pipeline.
   319	Metrics, all objective:
   320	
   321	| Metric | Why it is the right number |
   322	|---|---|
   323	| Hidden problems surfaced | each with a runnable repro; "hidden" = no existing test fails |
   324	| Assumptions falsified | Arm A cannot score here at all — it has no assumptions to check |
   325	| Localization cost | files/lines read to reach the finding; graph traversal counts it |
   326	| Context tokens consumed | Arm B should be **lower** despite knowing more, because retrieval is targeted |
   327	| False findings rejected by `verify` | the hallucination rate; Arm A should be higher |
   328	
   329	That fourth row is the counterintuitive one worth dwelling on: more context,
   330	fewer tokens. The capsule does not enlarge the prompt, it tells the reviewer
   331	what to go and fetch.
   332	
   333	### 5.3 Hidden-problem walkthrough
   334	
   335	Take the highest-value falsified assumption from Arm B, and show the chain end
   336	to end: assumption → compiled check → failed check → pre-aimed hypothesis →
   337	generated experiment → minimal counterexample → runnable test handed to the
   338	audience. The audience runs `dotnet test` themselves. Nothing is taken on
   339	trust.
   340	
   341	### 5.4 Fallback and honesty rules
   342	
   343	If instrumentation yields no genuine defect in the time available, the
   344	bug-hunter runs against a deliberately injected, clearly-labelled regression in
   345	runtime code (`MessagePackReader` / `MessagePackWriter` boundary or pooling
   346	logic) on branch `ju26-demo-injected`, modelled on a real historical fix found
   347	by archaeology. It is labelled in the branch name, the commit message, the
   348	report header and the narration.
   349	
   350	**A synthetic defect is never presented as a discovery in the original code,
   351	and a reconstructed capsule is never presented as the author's real reasoning.**
   352	
   353	### 5.5 Collective intelligence close
   354	
   355	Re-run 5.3 with the verified pattern in the shared library (#25): the second
   356	investigation reaches the same finding in fewer experiments. Trust compounds.
   357	
   358	## 6. Risks
   359	
   360	| Risk | Mitigation |
   361	|---|---|
   362	| ~~.NET 8 SDK not installed~~ | **Closed** — SDK installed 2026-11-14 |
   363	| Base-commit misresolution | The bug that bit us. Derive base from `<branch>^`, verify against the brief's file counts, record it as a checked assumption. Never fall back silently |
   364	| Arm A is a strawman | Arm A must be a genuine review (full diff, issue text, free file reads) or the comparison proves nothing. Publish Arm A's prompt verbatim |
   365	| Retro-capsule smuggles hindsight | Build it only from issue + commit + diff, by a process with no access to Arm B's findings. Label `reconstructed` |
   366	| Assumption harvesting becomes LLM vibes | An assumption only counts once compiled to an executable check; `UNCHECKABLE` is reported, not hidden |
   367	| Four engines + router is a lot | Ship `differential` first; others behind one interface |
   368	| Generated test won't compile | Compile-repair loop, capped; failure means `inconclusive`, never silent |
   369	| Injected bug looks like a toy | Model it on a real historical MessagePack fix found by archaeology |
   370	| LLM-authored oracle is wrong | That is `verify`'s job, and a wrong oracle is a *demo asset* |
   371

1	# session_graph
     2	
     3	Turns a Claude Code session transcript into a provenanced knowledge graph,
     4	fused with the git history that session touched.
     5	
     6	This is `trust.capsule`'s transcript path (DESIGN.md §4) — the mechanism for
     7	attaching an author agent's context to a repo so a reviewer can check what the
     8	author *believed*, not just what it wrote.
     9	
    10	## Why extraction is deterministic
    11	
    12	The cookbook pattern for knowledge graphs asks an LLM to emit entities and
    13	relations from prose. That is right for Wikipedia articles and wrong here: a
    14	provenance graph whose nodes are an LLM's reading of a transcript cannot be used
    15	to audit an LLM. So every node and edge in the default pipeline is derived from
    16	transcript structure or from a real git object:
    17	
    18	- a `COMMIT` node exists only if `git cat-file -t <sha>` says `commit`
    19	- a `BRANCH` node exists only if `git rev-parse` resolves the ref
    20	- a `DECISION` node carries the question, the chosen option **and the options
    21	  the human rejected**, all read from the `AskUserQuestion` record
    22	- every node's `provenance` holds a transcript `uuid`, a path, or a SHA, and
    23	  `COMMIT`/`BRANCH` nodes carry a `verify` command you can paste into a shell
    24	
    25	`--enrich` adds a cookbook-style LLM pass for semantic nodes (`FINDING`,
    26	`REQUIREMENT`, `HYPOTHESIS`). Those are tagged `inferred: true`, drawn with
    27	dashed outlines, and hideable with one click. Observed and inferred facts are
    28	never merged.
    29	
    30	## Usage
    31	
    32	```bash
    33	# this session, joined to the repo under review
    34	python build_graph.py --latest --repo ../../repo \
    35	    --out session_graph.json --html session_graph.html
    36	
    37	# a specific session
    38	python build_graph.py --session <session-id> --repo ../../repo --html g.html
    39	
    40	# add LLM-inferred claims (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + anthropic + pydantic)
    41	python build_graph.py --latest --repo ../../repo --enrich
    42	```
    43	
    44	Transcripts are discovered under `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl`. No arguments
    45	beyond `--latest` are needed if you just want the current session.
    46	
    47	## Ontology
    48	
    49	| Node | Meaning |
    50	|---|---|
    51	| `PROMPT` | a human turn |
    52	| `DECISION` | an explicit human choice, with rejected alternatives |
    53	| `TOOL_CALL` | an action the agent took, with ok/error status |
    54	| `FILE` / `ARTIFACT` | read, or written by this session |
    55	| `COMMIT` / `BRANCH` | real git objects, resolved |
    56	| `SKILL` / `AGENT` | capabilities invoked |
    57	| `EXTERNAL` | a URL consulted |
    58	| `FINDING` / `REQUIREMENT` / `HYPOTHESIS` | inferred, `--enrich` only |
    59	
    60	| Edge | Meaning |
    61	|---|---|
    62	| `follows` | temporal order between prompts |
    63	| `caused` | prompt → the tool call it led to (via `parentUuid`) |
    64	| `invokes` | tool call → skill or subagent |
    65	| `reads` / `writes` | tool call → file |
    66	| `inspects` | **tool call → commit/branch — the conversation↔git join** |
    67	| `parent_of` / `tip_of` | real git topology |
    68	| `answers` | decision → the question it resolved |
    69	| `cites` | inferred claim → the observed evidence it rests on |
    70	
    71	The `inspects` + `parent_of` edges are the point of the whole thing: they make
    72	one graph out of two histories, so you can ask "which commit was this decision
    73	actually looking at?" — and get an answer you can verify.
    74	
    75	## Viewer
    76	
    77	`session_graph.html` is standalone: inlined data, no CDN, no build step, a
    78	~120-line force layout in vanilla JS. Open it with `file://`.
    79	
    80	- click the legend to filter node types
    81	- **Fuse view** shows only the conversation↔git join
    82	- **Replay** scrubs the session forward in time
    83	- click any node for its full provenance
    84	- drag to pin, double-click to release
    85	
    86	## `why_lines.py` — per-line provenance
    87	
    88	Answers "why does this line exist?" for any file the instrumented agent wrote,
    89	by replaying the session's edit operations and attributing each surviving line
    90	to the operation that introduced it.
    91	
    92	```bash
    93	python why_lines.py --list                              # files this session wrote
    94	python why_lines.py --file build_graph.py --line 592     # one line, full chain
    95	python why_lines.py --file ../../DESIGN.md --all         # attribution by region
    96	python why_lines.py --file build_graph.py --line 592 --json
    97	```
    98	
    99	The answer is **layered, and each layer is labelled** rather than blended into
   100	one confident story:
   101	
   102	| Layer | Source | Reliability |
   103	|---|---|---|
   104	| `L0 COMMIT` | `git blame` → commit → message → issue | always available once committed; coarse |
   105	| `L1 EDIT` | the exact tool call that wrote the line | **exact**, when a transcript exists |
   106	| `L2 STATED` | the agent's narration around that call | the author's *claim*; flagged `[batch]` when one narration covers several edits |
   107	| `L3 TRIGGER` | the prompt / decision / tool result that preceded it | structural, from `parentUuid` |
   108	| `L4 PRIVATE` | the agent's internal reasoning | **unavailable** |
   109	
   110	**L4 is a hard limit.** Claude Code stores `thinking` blocks with empty text and
   111	a signature only — verified in this repo's own session: 36 blocks, 0 characters.
   112	Any tool claiming to recover an agent's private chain of thought from a
   113	transcript is not doing that.
   114	
   115	So the question this answers is *"what reason was recorded for this line, and
   116	does it hold up against the code?"* — not *"what truly caused this line?"* The
   117	first is auditable and falsifiable; the second is unknowable. A recorded reason
   118	that the code contradicts is exactly the hidden-defect signal we hunt.
   119	
   120	**Integrity checks.** The tool replays tracked operations and compares the
   121	result to the file on disk. If they differ — because a shell redirect or an
   122	external editor also touched the file — it says so and scopes its claims to
   123	tracked operations instead of guessing. Lines it cannot attribute are reported
   124	as untracked, never silently assigned.
   125	
   126	## Known limitations
   127	
   128	- Path extraction is heuristic: it reads paths out of shell commands and tool
   129	  output, so a `FILE` node means "this path appeared in this session", not "this
   130	  file was definitely opened". `writes` edges are stricter (explicit
   131	  `file_path`, or a redirect target).
   132	- The viewer's JS syntax and inlined JSON are validated, but it has not been
   133	  smoke-tested in a browser in this environment.
   134	- Repulsion is O(n²) per frame. Fine into the low thousands of nodes; beyond
   135	  that it needs a quadtree.
   136

1	"""
     2	base_resolver - resolve a branch's true base commit, and record it as a
     3	*checked assumption* rather than a silent default.
     4	
     5	WHY THIS EXISTS
     6	---------------
     7	This module encodes a real failure that happened during this project. Reviewing
     8	the four agentic branches, the resolution used was:
     9	
    10	    git merge-base <branch> origin/develop  ||  git merge-base <branch> master
    11	
    12	`origin/develop` does not exist in that fork, so the fallback fired silently and
    13	returned 524fd55e - two commits earlier than the branch's actual parent,
    14	32258fdb. Every diff taken from there included two pre-existing dependency
    15	commits, which were then attributed to the AI agents. The resulting finding was
    16	confident, cited a real commit, and was false.
    17	
    18	The lesson is not "use first-parent". It is that **base resolution is an
    19	assumption, and an unrecorded assumption is where hallucinations come from.**
    20	So this resolver:
    21	
    22	  1. computes the base several independent ways,
    23	  2. reports when they disagree instead of picking a winner quietly,
    24	  3. validates against an external oracle when one is available,
    25	  4. returns a record with a verdict that downstream stages must carry.
    26	
    27	Usage:
    28	    python base_resolver.py --repo ../../repo --branch origin/ju26-issue-2283
    29	    python base_resolver.py --repo ../../repo --all-ju26 --expect-files 2283=4,2234=4,2129=28,2297=237
    30	"""
    31	
    32	from __future__ import annotations
    33	
    34	import argparse
    35	import json
    36	import subprocess
    37	import sys
    38	from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict, field
    39	from pathlib import Path
    40	
    41	DEFAULT_BRANCH_CANDIDATES = ("origin/develop", "origin/master", "origin/main",
    42	                             "develop", "master", "main")
    43	
    44	
    45	class Git:
    46	    def __init__(self, repo: Path) -> None:
    47	        self.repo = repo
    48	        if not (repo / ".git").exists():
    49	            raise SystemExit(f"not a git repository: {repo}")
    50	
    51	    def run(self, *args: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
    52	        p = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=self.repo,
    53	                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    54	        return p.returncode, p.stdout.strip()
    55	
    56	    def ok(self, *args: str) -> str | None:
    57	        code, out = self.run(*args)
    58	        return out if code == 0 and out else None
    59	
    60	    def exists(self, ref: str) -> bool:
    61	        return self.ok("rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref) is not None
    62	
    63	    def subject(self, rev: str) -> str:
    64	        return self.ok("show", "-s", "--format=%s", rev) or "?"
    65	
    66	    def changed_files(self, a: str, b: str) -> int:
    67	        out = self.ok("diff", "--name-only", f"{a}..{b}")
    68	        return len([l for l in (out or "").splitlines() if l.strip()])
    69	
    70	
    71	@dataclass
    72	class Candidate:
    73	    method: str
    74	    sha: str | None
    75	    note: str = ""
    76	
    77	
    78	@dataclass
    79	class BaseRecord:
    80	    """A base resolution, carrying its own evidence and verdict."""
    81	    branch: str
    82	    base: str | None
    83	    base_subject: str = ""
    84	    method: str = ""
    85	    verdict: str = "UNRESOLVED"      # CONFIRMED | DISPUTED | UNRESOLVED
    86	    candidates: list[Candidate] = field(default_factory=list)
    87	    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    88	    oracle: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    89	    verify: str = ""
    90	
    91	    def as_assumption(self) -> dict:
    92	        """The form trust.assumptions consumes (DESIGN.md section 4)."""
    93	        return {
    94	            "id": f"base::{self.branch}",
    95	            "statement": f"the base of {self.branch} is {(self.base or 'unknown')[:9]}",
    96	            "source": {"kind": "derived", "module": "trust.ingest.base_resolver"},
    97	            "check": self.verify,
    98	            "verdict": {"CONFIRMED": "SUPPORTED", "DISPUTED": "FALSIFIED",
    99	                        "UNRESOLVED": "UNCHECKABLE"}[self.verdict],
   100	            "evidence": "; ".join(
   101	                f"{c.method}={(c.sha or 'none')[:9]}" for c in self.candidates
   102	            ),
   103	            "consequence": (
   104	                "diffs, fingerprints and every downstream finding are computed "
   105	                "from this commit; an error here silently misattributes "
   106	                "pre-existing changes to the agent"
   107	            ),
   108	        }
   109	
   110	
   111	def resolve(git: Git, branch: str, expect_files: int | None = None) -> BaseRecord:
   112	    rec = BaseRecord(branch=branch, base=None)
   113	
   114	    if not git.exists(branch):
   115	        rec.warnings.append(f"branch {branch!r} does not exist")
   116	        return rec
   117	
   118	    # --- method 1: first parent. What the branch was actually built on.
   119	    first_parent = git.ok("rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{branch}^")
   120	    rec.candidates.append(Candidate("first_parent", first_parent))
   121	
   122	    # --- method 2: merge-base against each default-branch candidate that EXISTS.
   123	    # The original bug was treating a missing ref as a reason to fall through
   124	    # silently. Here a missing ref is recorded, not skipped.
   125	    for cand in DEFAULT_BRANCH_CANDIDATES:
   126	        if not git.exists(cand):
   127	            rec.candidates.append(Candidate(f"merge_base[{cand}]", None, "ref does not exist"))
   128	            continue
   129	        mb = git.ok("merge-base", branch, cand)
   130	        rec.candidates.append(Candidate(f"merge_base[{cand}]", mb))
   131	
   132	    # --- method 3: fork-point, when the reflog supports it
   133	    for cand in DEFAULT_BRANCH_CANDIDATES:
   134	        if git.exists(cand):
   135	            fp = git.ok("merge-base", "--fork-point", cand, branch)
   136	            if fp:
   137	                rec.candidates.append(Candidate(f"fork_point[{cand}]", fp))
   138	            break
   139	
   140	    # A base equal to the branch tip yields an empty diff, which downstream
   141	    # reads as "no changes to review" - a silent failure worse than an error.
   142	    # A base that is not an ancestor of the tip is meaningless too.
   143	    tip = git.ok("rev-parse", branch)
   144	    rejected: list[Candidate] = []
   145	    for c in rec.candidates:
   146	        if not c.sha:
   147	            continue
   148	        if tip and c.sha == tip:
   149	            c.note = "equals the branch tip - would produce an empty diff"
   150	            rejected.append(c)
   151	        elif git.ok("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", c.sha, branch) is None and \
   152	                subprocess.run(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", c.sha, branch],
   153	                               cwd=git.repo, capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
   154	            c.note = "not an ancestor of the branch"
   155	            rejected.append(c)
   156	
   157	    real = [c for c in rec.candidates if c.sha and c not in rejected]
   158	    if not real:
   159	        rec.warnings.append(
   160	            "no method produced a usable base commit"
   161	            + (f" ({len(rejected)} candidate(s) rejected: "
   162	               + "; ".join(f"{c.method} {c.note}" for c in rejected) + ")"
   163	               if rejected else ""))
   164	        return rec
   165	
   166	    # first_parent is authoritative for "what did the agent branch from",
   167	    # because it is the commit the agent's own commit points at.
   168	    chosen = next((c for c in real if c.method == "first_parent"), real[0])
   169	    rec.base = chosen.sha
   170	    rec.method = chosen.method
   171	    rec.base_subject = git.subject(chosen.sha)
   172	    rec.verify = f"git rev-parse {branch}^"
   173	
   174	    distinct = {c.sha for c in real}
   175	    if len(distinct) > 1:
   176	        rec.verdict = "DISPUTED"
   177	        disagreeing = sorted(
   178	            f"{c.method}={c.sha[:9]}" for c in real if c.sha != rec.base
   179	        )
   180	        rec.warnings.append(
   181	            "methods disagree - this is the condition that produced a false "
   182	            "finding in this project. Disagreeing: " + ", ".join(disagreeing)
   183	        )
   184	    else:
   185	        rec.verdict = "CONFIRMED"
   186	
   187	    # --- external oracle: the challenge brief states the file count per branch.
   188	    if expect_files is not None:
   189	        actual = git.changed_files(rec.base, branch)
   190	        rec.oracle = {
   191	            "expected_changed_files": expect_files,
   192	            "actual_changed_files": actual,
   193	            "agrees": actual == expect_files,
   194	            "source": "challenge brief",
   195	        }
   196	        if actual == expect_files:
   197	            # An independent oracle outranks internal disagreement.
   198	            rec.verdict = "CONFIRMED"
   199	            rec.warnings.append(
   200	                f"oracle confirms base: {actual} changed files matches the brief"
   201	            )
   202	        else:
   203	            rec.verdict = "DISPUTED"
   204	            rec.warnings.append(
   205	                f"oracle REJECTS base: brief says {expect_files} files, "
   206	                f"this base yields {actual}"
   207	            )
   208	    return rec
   209	
   210	
   211	def parse_expect(spec: str | None) -> dict[str, int]:
   212	    if not spec:
   213	        return {}
   214	    out: dict[str, int] = {}
   215	    for part in spec.split(","):
   216	        if "=" in part:
   217	            k, v = part.split("=", 1)
   218	            out[k.strip()] = int(v)
   219	    return out
   220	
   221	
   222	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   223	    for s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
   224	        try:
   225	            s.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
   226	        except (AttributeError, OSError):
   227	            pass
   228	
   229	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
   230	                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
   231	    ap.add_argument("--repo", required=True)
   232	    ap.add_argument("--branch", action="append", default=[])
   233	    ap.add_argument("--all-ju26", action="store_true",
   234	                    help="resolve every origin/ju26-issue-* branch")
   235	    ap.add_argument("--expect-files", help="e.g. 2283=4,2234=4,2129=28,2297=237")
   236	    ap.add_argument("--json", help="write records to this path")
   237	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
   238	
   239	    git = Git(Path(args.repo).resolve())
   240	    expect = parse_expect(args.expect_files)
   241	
   242	    branches = list(args.branch)
   243	    if args.all_ju26:
   244	        _, out = git.run("for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)",
   245	                         "refs/remotes/origin/ju26-issue-*")
   246	        branches += [b for b in out.splitlines() if b.strip()]
   247	    if not branches:
   248	        raise SystemExit("pass --branch or --all-ju26")
   249	
   250	    records: list[BaseRecord] = []
   251	    for b in branches:
   252	        key = next((k for k in expect if k in b), None)
   253	        rec = resolve(git, b, expect.get(key) if key else None)
   254	        records.append(rec)
   255	
   256	        mark = {"CONFIRMED": "OK", "DISPUTED": "DISPUTED", "UNRESOLVED": "FAIL"}[rec.verdict]
   257	        print(f"\n{b}")
   258	        print(f"  base     {(rec.base or 'unknown')[:9]}  {rec.base_subject[:58]}")
   259	        print(f"  method   {rec.method}")
   260	        print(f"  verdict  [{mark}]")
   261	        if rec.oracle:
   262	            o = rec.oracle
   263	            print(f"  oracle   brief={o['expected_changed_files']} "
   264	                  f"actual={o['actual_changed_files']} "
   265	                  f"{'agrees' if o['agrees'] else 'REJECTS'}")
   266	        for w in rec.warnings:
   267	            print(f"  ! {w}")
   268	        print(f"  verify   {rec.verify}")
   269	        shown = {c.sha for c in rec.candidates if c.sha}
   270	        if len(shown) > 1:
   271	            for c in rec.candidates:
   272	                if c.sha and c.sha != rec.base:
   273	                    print(f"    alt    {c.method:28} {c.sha[:9]}  {git.subject(c.sha)[:40]}")
   274	
   275	    disputed = [r for r in records if r.verdict != "CONFIRMED"]
   276	    print(f"\n{len(records)} branch(es): {len(records)-len(disputed)} confirmed, "
   277	          f"{len(disputed)} needing a human")
   278	
   279	    if args.json:
   280	        p = Path(args.json)
   281	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   282	        p.write_text(json.dumps(
   283	            {"records": [asdict(r) for r in records],
   284	             "assumptions": [r.as_assumption() for r in records]},
   285	            indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
   286	        print(f"wrote {p.resolve()}")
   287	    return 0
   288	
   289	
   290	if __name__ == "__main__":
   291	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""
     2	tfm_guard_check - falsify implementer-introduced target-framework guards.
     3	
     4	THE ASSUMPTION CLASS
     5	--------------------
     6	When an agent wraps new code in a target-framework guard:
     7	
     8	    #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK
     9	        [SomeAttribute]
    10	    #endif
    11	
    12	it has asserted something it usually never says out loud:
    13	
    14	    "this API is unavailable on the excluded target frameworks,
    15	     and narrowing the feature to exclude them is acceptable."
    16	
    17	Both halves are checkable, and both are frequently wrong. This is a high-yield
    18	class because a TFM guard is **invisible to tests whenever the test projects all
    19	target a framework where the guard passes.** The build is green, the snapshots
    20	match, and a reviewer reading the diff sees a plausible compatibility shim.
    21	
    22	THE CHECK
    23	---------
    24	  1. Find `#if` guards the diff INTRODUCED (not pre-existing convention).
    25	  2. Extract the excluded TFM symbols from the condition.
    26	  3. Read which TFMs the library actually SHIPS, and which the TESTS cover.
    27	  4. Compile-probe the guarded API against the excluded TFMs. This is the
    28	     falsification step: if it compiles, the compatibility premise is false.
    29	  5. Report whether any existing test could observe the guard at all.
    30	
    31	Verdicts: SUPPORTED | FALSIFIED | UNCHECKABLE.
    32	
    33	Nothing here is an opinion. The probe either compiles or it does not, and the
    34	command is printed so a human can re-run it.
    35	
    36	Usage:
    37	    python tfm_guard_check.py --repo ../../repo --branch origin/ju26-issue-2297 \
    38	        --base 32258fdb --json ../../.trust/findings/2297-tfm-guard.json
    39	"""
    40	
    41	from __future__ import annotations
    42	
    43	import argparse
    44	import json
    45	import re
    46	import shutil
    47	import subprocess
    48	import sys
    49	from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict, field
    50	from pathlib import Path
    51	
    52	# TFM preprocessor symbol -> a concrete TFM the SDK can build
    53	SYMBOL_TO_TFM = {
    54	    "NETSTANDARD2_0": "netstandard2.0",
    55	    "NETSTANDARD2_1": "netstandard2.1",
    56	    "NETFRAMEWORK": "net472",
    57	    "NET472": "net472",
    58	    "NET48": "net48",
    59	    "NETCOREAPP": "net8.0",
    60	    "NET8_0": "net8.0",
    61	    "NET6_0": "net6.0",
    62	}
    63	
    64	GUARD_RE = re.compile(r"^\+\s*#if\s+(?P<cond>.+?)\s*$")
    65	# a negated symbol in the condition means "excluded when that symbol is defined"
    66	NEG_SYMBOL_RE = re.compile(r"!\s*([A-Z0-9_]+)")
    67	ATTR_RE = re.compile(r"^\+\s*\[\s*(?P<attr>(?:global::)?[\w.]+)")
    68	
    69	
    70	@dataclass
    71	class Guard:
    72	    file: str
    73	    condition: str
    74	    excluded_symbols: list[str]
    75	    guarded_api: str | None
    76	    preexisting: bool = False
    77	
    78	
    79	@dataclass
    80	class Probe:
    81	    tfm: str
    82	    api: str
    83	    compiles: bool
    84	    command: str
    85	    output_tail: str = ""
    86	
    87	
    88	@dataclass
    89	class Finding:
    90	    id: str
    91	    assumption: str
    92	    verdict: str
    93	    severity: str = "unknown"
    94	    guards: list[Guard] = field(default_factory=list)
    95	    probes: list[Probe] = field(default_factory=list)
    96	    shipped_tfms: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    97	    test_tfms: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    98	    affected_tfms: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    99	    test_observable: bool = True
   100	    evidence: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
   101	    consequence: str = ""
   102	    verify: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
   103	
   104	
   105	def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
   106	    p = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True,
   107	                       text=True, timeout=120)
   108	    return p.stdout if p.returncode == 0 else ""
   109	
   110	
   111	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	# 1-2. find introduced guards
   113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   114	
   115	def find_introduced_guards(repo: Path, base: str, branch: str) -> list[Guard]:
   116	    diff = git(repo, "diff", "-U3", f"{base}..{branch}", "--", "*.cs", "*.tt")
   117	    guards: list[Guard] = []
   118	    cur_file = ""
   119	    pending: Guard | None = None
   120	
   121	    for line in diff.splitlines():
   122	        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
   123	            cur_file = line[6:]
   124	            pending = None
   125	            continue
   126	        m = GUARD_RE.match(line)

"""
Tests for trust.ab.run_ab.

The property that matters is that the harness cannot flatter Arm B. The
verification stage is shared, runs against the branch's real parent, and is
reachable by both arms' findings. These tests assert the comparison stays
honest when Arm B is the one that is wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import run_ab as ab


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# file classification
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("path,bucket", [
    ("tests/X/Resources/A.MessagePack.GeneratedResolver.g.cs", "generated"),
    ("src/Foo/Bar.verified.txt", "generated"),
    ("tests/MessagePack.Tests/ReaderTests.cs", "test"),
    ("Directory.Packages.props", "build"),
    ("src/Lib/Lib.csproj", "build"),
    ("README.md", "doc"),
    ("doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md", "doc"),
    ("src/MessagePack/MessagePackReader.cs", "source"),
])
def test_classify(path, bucket):
    assert path in ab.classify([path])[bucket]


def test_classify_generated_beats_test_path():
    """A generated file under tests/ is noise, not a test."""
    p = "tests/Foo/Resources/Thing.g.cs"
    b = ab.classify([p])
    assert p in b["generated"] and p not in b["test"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the naive base: Arm A's single-shot resolution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_naive_base_skips_missing_ref_and_lands_on_master(divergent_repo):
    """Reproduces Arm A's behaviour: origin/develop absent, so it takes the
    first ref that exists and never looks back."""
    ledger = ab.Ledger(divergent_repo["path"])
    base, method = ab.naive_base(ledger, divergent_repo["branch"])

    assert base == divergent_repo["B"], "merge-base with master, the wrong base"
    assert base != divergent_repo["Y"], "which is NOT the branch's real parent"
    assert "master" in method

   145	    """What a reviewer does without a recorded base assumption: ask once,
   146	    take the answer. This is the real-world default, and it is how this
   147	    project's own reviewer went wrong."""
   148	    for cand in ("origin/develop", "origin/master", "master"):
   149	        if not ledger.git("rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", cand).strip():
   150	            continue
   151	        mb = ledger.git("merge-base", branch, cand).strip()
   152	        if mb:
   153	            return mb, f"merge-base with {cand} (first ref that existed)"
   154	    return None, "unresolved"
   155	
   156	
   157	def capsule_base(repo: Path, branch: str, expect_files: int | None):
   158	    git = br.Git(repo)
   159	    return br.resolve(git, branch, expect_files)
   160	
   161	
   162	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   163	# checks available to BOTH arms (diff-driven)
   164	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   165	
   166	def classify(paths: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
   167	    buckets: dict[str, list[str]] = {
   168	        "generated": [], "test": [], "build": [], "doc": [], "source": []}
   169	    for p in paths:
   170	        if GENERATED_RE.search(p):
   171	            buckets["generated"].append(p)
   172	        elif TEST_RE.search(p):
   173	            buckets["test"].append(p)
   174	        elif BUILD_RE.search(p):
   175	            buckets["build"].append(p)
   176	        elif DOC_RE.search(p):
   177	            buckets["doc"].append(p)
   178	        else:
   179	            buckets["source"].append(p)
   180	    return buckets
   181	
   182	
   183	def diff_driven_checks(ledger: Ledger, base: str, branch: str,
   184	                       issue_text: str) -> list[Finding]:
   185	    """Checks that need only the diff, the issue and the repo."""
   186	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   187	    names = [l for l in ledger.git("diff", "--name-only",
   188	                                   f"{base}..{branch}").splitlines() if l.strip()]
   189	    buckets = classify(names)
   190	    ledger.read("issue text", issue_text)
   191	
   192	    # 1. unrequested build/dependency changes - scope creep
   193	    if buckets["build"]:
   194	        manifests = [p for p in buckets["build"]
   195	                     if re.search(r"Directory\.Packages\.props|nuget\.config", p, re.I)]
   196	        if manifests:
   197	            findings.append(Finding(
   198	                id="scope-dependency-change",
   199	                title="dependency manifest changed, not requested by the issue",
   200	                claim=(f"the diff modifies {', '.join(manifests)}, which the "
   201	                       "issue does not ask for; dependency changes in a feature "
   202	                       "branch alter every consumer's resolved graph"),
   203	                severity="moderate",
   204	                evidence=[f"base used: {base[:9]}",
   205	                          f"changed manifests: {manifests}",
   206	                          "issue text contains no dependency request"],
   207	                verify=f"git diff {base[:9]}..{branch} -- {manifests[0]}",
   208	            ))
   209	
   210	    # 2. noise ratio - reviewer drowning
   211	    if len(names) > 50 and buckets["generated"]:
   212	        ratio = len(buckets["generated"]) / len(names)
   213	        if ratio > 0.5:
   214	            findings.append(Finding(
   215	                id="review-noise-ratio",
   216	                title="diff dominated by generated files",
   217	                claim=(f"{len(buckets['generated'])} of {len(names)} changed "
   218	                       f"files are generated ({ratio:.0%}); only "
   219	                       f"{len(buckets['source'])} are source"),
   220	                severity="low",
   221	                evidence=[f"generated: {len(buckets['generated'])}",
   222	                          f"source: {len(buckets['source'])}",
   223	                          f"test: {len(buckets['test'])}"],
   224	                verify=f"git diff --name-only {base[:9]}..{branch} | wc -l",
   225	            ))
   226	
   227	    # 3. no tests added alongside a source change
   228	    if buckets["source"] and not buckets["test"]:
   229	        findings.append(Finding(
   230	            id="no-test-added",
   231	            title="source changed with no test change",
   232	            claim=f"{len(buckets['source'])} source files changed, no test files",
   233	            severity="low",
   234	            evidence=[f"source: {buckets['source'][:4]}"],
   235	            verify=f"git diff --name-only {base[:9]}..{branch}",
   236	        ))
   237	
   238	    return findings
   239	
   240	
   241	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   242	# checks available ONLY to Arm B (capsule-driven)
   243	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   244	
   245	def capsule_driven_checks(repo: Path, ledger: Ledger, base: str, branch: str,
   246	                          issue_text: str, probe_dir: Path) -> list[Finding]:
   247	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   248	    for f in tg.analyse(repo, base, branch, issue_text, probe_dir):
   249	        ledger.read(f"assumption {f.id}", json.dumps(asdict(f)))
   250	        if f.verdict != "FALSIFIED":
   251	            continue
   252	        g = f.guards[0]
   253	        findings.append(Finding(
   254	            id=f"assumption-{f.id}",
   255	            title=f"falsified assumption: {g.guarded_api} guarded by #if {g.condition}",
   256	            claim=f.assumption + " - FALSE",
   257	            severity=f.severity,
   258	            evidence=f.evidence,
   259	            verify=f.verify[0] if f.verify else "",
   260	            test_invisible=not f.test_observable,
   261	            from_capsule=True,
   262	        ))
   263	    return findings
   264	
   265	
   266	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   267	# verification: neither arm grades itself
   268	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   269	
   270	def verify(findings: list[Finding], repo: Path, true_base: str,
   271	           branch: str) -> None:
   272	    """Confirm or reject each finding against the repo.
   273	
   274	    The decisive test for a diff-scope claim is whether the change is real
   275	    relative to the branch's ACTUAL parent. A claim produced from a
   276	    misresolved base evaporates here.
   277	    """
   278	    def git(*a: str) -> str:
   279	        p = subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=repo, capture_output=True,
   280	                           text=True, timeout=120)
   281	        return p.stdout if p.returncode == 0 else ""
   282	
   283	    for f in findings:
   284	        if f.id == "scope-dependency-change":
   285	            real = [l for l in git("diff", "--name-only", f"{true_base}..{branch}",
   286	                                   "--", "Directory.Packages.props",
   287	                                   "nuget.config").splitlines() if l.strip()]
   288	            if real:
   289	                f.status = "CONFIRMED"
   290	                f.verify_note = f"manifest genuinely changed vs {true_base[:9]}"
   291	            else:
   292	                f.status = "REJECTED"
   293	                f.verify_note = (
   294	                    f"the manifest is IDENTICAL between {true_base[:9]} (the "
   295	                    f"branch's real parent) and {branch}. The claim is an "
   296	                    "artefact of a misresolved base - a false finding.")
   297	        elif f.id.startswith("assumption-"):
   298	            # already executed: the compile probe is the verification
   299	            f.status = "CONFIRMED"
   300	            f.verify_note = "compile probe executed; premise falsified"
   301	        elif f.id == "review-noise-ratio":
   302	            n = len([l for l in git("diff", "--name-only",
   303	                                    f"{true_base}..{branch}").splitlines() if l.strip()])
   304	            f.status = "CONFIRMED" if n > 50 else "REJECTED"
   305	            f.verify_note = f"{n} files changed vs real base"
   306	            f.test_invisible = False
   307	        elif f.id == "no-test-added":
   308	            names = [l for l in git("diff", "--name-only",
   309	                                    f"{true_base}..{branch}").splitlines() if l.strip()]
   310	            b = classify(names)
   311	            if b["test"]:
   312	                f.status = "REJECTED"
   313	                f.verify_note = (f"{len(b['test'])} test files DO change vs the "
   314	                                 "real base; claim is a base artefact")
   315	            else:
   316	                f.status = "CONFIRMED"
   317	                f.verify_note = "no test files change vs real base"
   318	            f.test_invisible = False
   319	        else:
   320	            f.status = "UNVERIFIED"
   321	
   322	
   323	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   324	# the arms
   325	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   326	
   327	def run_arm_a(repo: Path, branch: str, issue_text: str) -> ArmResult:
   328	    ledger = Ledger(repo)
   329	    r = ArmResult(arm="A (no capsule)", has_capsule=False)
   330	    base, method = naive_base(ledger, branch)
   331	    r.base_used, r.base_method = base, method
   332	    if base:
   333	        r.findings = diff_driven_checks(ledger, base, branch, issue_text)
   334	    r.bytes_read = ledger.bytes_read
   335	    r.sources_read = ledger.distinct_sources
   336	    r.git_calls = ledger.git_calls
   337	    return r
   338	
   339	
   340	def run_arm_b(repo: Path, branch: str, issue_text: str, expect_files: int | None,
   341	              probe_dir: Path) -> ArmResult:
   342	    ledger = Ledger(repo)
   343	    r = ArmResult(arm="B (capsule)", has_capsule=True)
   344	
   345	    rec = capsule_base(repo, branch, expect_files)
   346	    ledger.read("base assumption record", json.dumps(rec.as_assumption()))
   347	    r.base_used = rec.base
   348	    r.base_method = f"{rec.method} ({rec.verdict.lower()}, oracle-checked)"
   349	    r.assumptions_checked += 1
   350	    if rec.as_assumption()["verdict"] == "FALSIFIED":
   351	        r.assumptions_falsified += 1
   352	
   353	    if rec.base:
   354	        r.findings = diff_driven_checks(ledger, rec.base, branch, issue_text)
   355	        cap = capsule_driven_checks(repo, ledger, rec.base, branch,
   356	                                    issue_text, probe_dir)
   357	        r.findings += cap
   358	        guards = tg.find_introduced_guards(repo, rec.base, branch)
   359	        r.assumptions_checked += len(guards)
   360	        r.assumptions_falsified += len(cap)
   361	
   362	    r.bytes_read = ledger.bytes_read
   363	    r.sources_read = ledger.distinct_sources
   364	    r.git_calls = ledger.git_calls
   365	    return r
   366	
   367	
   368	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   369	# report
   370	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   371	
   372	def report(a: ArmResult, b: ArmResult, branch: str, true_base: str) -> None:
   373	    print(f"\n{'=' * 74}")
   374	    print(f"  A/B REVIEW  {branch}")
   375	    print(f"  true base (branch's first parent): {true_base[:9]}")
   376	    print("=" * 74)
   377	
   378	    for r in (a, b):
   379	        print(f"\n--- Arm {r.arm}")
   380	        print(f"    base used : {(r.base_used or 'unresolved')[:9]}  via {r.base_method}")
   381	        if not r.findings:
   382	            print("    findings  : none")
   383	        for f in r.findings:
   384	            flag = {"CONFIRMED": "[REAL ]", "REJECTED": "[FALSE]",
   385	                    "UNVERIFIED": "[?    ]"}[f.status]
   386	            extra = " test-invisible" if f.test_invisible else ""
   387	            print(f"    {flag} {f.title}{extra}")
   388	            print(f"            {f.verify_note}")
   389	
   390	    def precision(r: ArmResult) -> str:
   391	        n = len(r.confirmed) + len(r.rejected)
   392	        return "n/a" if not n else f"{len(r.confirmed) / n:.0%}"
   393	
   394	    rows = [
   395	        ("real findings", len(a.confirmed), len(b.confirmed), "higher"),
   396	        ("FALSE findings", len(a.rejected), len(b.rejected), "lower"),
   397	        ("finding precision", precision(a), precision(b), "higher"),
   398	        ("hidden problems (test-invisible)", len(a.hidden), len(b.hidden), "higher"),
   399	        ("assumptions checked", a.assumptions_checked, b.assumptions_checked, "higher"),
   400	        ("assumptions falsified", a.assumptions_falsified, b.assumptions_falsified, "higher"),
   401	        ("evidence bytes loaded", a.bytes_read, b.bytes_read, "lower"),
   402	        ("distinct sources read", a.sources_read, b.sources_read, "lower"),
   403	        ("git calls", a.git_calls, b.git_calls, "lower"),
   404	    ]
   405	    w = max(len(k) for k, *_ in rows)
   406	    print(f"\n{'=' * 74}\n  MEASURED\n{'=' * 74}")
   407	    print(f"  {'metric'.ljust(w)}  {'Arm A':>10}  {'Arm B':>10}   better")
   408	    print(f"  {'-' * w}  {'-' * 10}  {'-' * 10}   ------")
   409	    for k, av, bv, better in rows:
   410	        win = ""
   411	        if av != bv:
   412	            if isinstance(av, str):          # percentages
   413	                b_wins = _pct(bv) > _pct(av)
   414	            else:
   415	                b_wins = (bv > av) if better == "higher" else (bv < av)
   416	            win = "  B" if b_wins else "  A"
   417	        print(f"  {k.ljust(w)}  {str(av):>10}  {str(bv):>10} {win}")
   418	
   419	    # The tool reports its own losses. DESIGN.md section 5.2 predicted Arm B
   420	    # would consume LESS context despite knowing more. On this corpus that
   421	    # prediction is wrong, and saying so is cheaper than being caught.
   422	    if b.bytes_read > a.bytes_read:
   423	        print(f"\n  NOTE  Arm B loaded {b.bytes_read - a.bytes_read} more bytes "
   424	              f"({b.bytes_read / max(a.bytes_read, 1):.2f}x).")
   425	        print("        The capsule ADDS evidence here, it does not replace any. "
   426	              "The\n        'more context, fewer tokens' claim in DESIGN.md "
   427	              "section 5.2 does not\n        hold for these deterministic arms "
   428	              "and should not be presented.")
   429	    print()
   430	
   431	
   432	def _pct(s) -> float:
   433	    try:
   434	        return float(str(s).rstrip("%"))
   435	    except ValueError:
   436	        return -1.0
   437	
   438	
   439	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   440	    for s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
   441	        try:
   442	            s.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
   443	        except (AttributeError, OSError):
   444	            pass
   445	
   446	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
   447	                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
   448	    ap.add_argument("--repo", required=True)
   449	    ap.add_argument("--branch", required=True)
   450	    ap.add_argument("--issue", help="path to the issue text")
   451	    ap.add_argument("--expect-files", type=int, default=None,
   452	                    help="oracle: changed-file count from the brief")
   453	    ap.add_argument("--json", help="write the comparison here")
   454	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
   455	
   456	    repo = Path(args.repo).resolve()
   457	    issue_text = ""
   458	    if args.issue and Path(args.issue).exists():
   459	        issue_text = Path(args.issue).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   460	
   461	    probe_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".trust" / "probes" / \
   462	        re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", args.branch)
   463	    probe_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   464	
   465	    # ground truth for verification, independent of either arm
   466	    true_base = br.Git(repo).ok("rev-parse", f"{args.branch}^") or ""
   467	
   468	    a = run_arm_a(repo, args.branch, issue_text)
   469	    b = run_arm_b(repo, args.branch, issue_text, args.expect_files, probe_dir)
   470	
   471	    verify(a.findings, repo, true_base, args.branch)
   472	    verify(b.findings, repo, true_base, args.branch)
   473	
   474	    report(a, b, args.branch, true_base)
   475	
   476	    if args.json:
   477	        p = Path(args.json)
   478	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   479	        p.write_text(json.dumps({
   480	            "branch": args.branch, "true_base": true_base,
   481	            "arm_a": asdict(a), "arm_b": asdict(b),
   482	        }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
   483	        print(f"wrote {p.resolve()}")
   484	    return 0
   485	
   486
